title: Transport Engines
summary: Proxy & Tunnel Engine Manager. The list shows every engine DayPass supports (Passwall, Passwall2, sing-box, Xray, WireGuard, OpenVPN), whether it is installed and running, how it intercepts traffic (self, tproxy or tunnel) and which one is active. Pick a number to open the engine.

items.title: Set as Active Engine
items.description: Saves the engine under /etc/daypass/transport/active_engine and re-applies the saved routing mode to it.
items.usage_tip: If the previous engine is still running you are asked to stop it, so two engines do not intercept the same traffic.

items.title: Start
items.description: Enables and starts the engine service (for WireGuard, brings the interface up).
items.usage_tip: Routing rules are not changed; apply a routing mode afterwards if needed.

items.title: Stop
items.description: Stops the engine service (for WireGuard, brings the interface down).
items.usage_tip: For sing-box/Xray the DayPass TPROXY rules stay loaded and LAN traffic stops working; choose Direct Only in Traffic Routing to go direct.

items.title: Restart
items.usage_tip: Use it after editing the engine config by hand.

items.title: Reload Rules
items.description: Reloads the engine and, for sing-box, Xray, WireGuard and OpenVPN, re-applies the saved routing mode.
items.usage_tip: Faster than a restart for rule changes.

items.title: Show Nodes / Endpoints
items.description: Lists the nodes (Passwall), outbounds (sing-box / Xray), peers (WireGuard) or instances (OpenVPN) and marks the active one.

items.title: Back
items.description: Returns to the engine list (and from there to the previous menu).

items.title: Quit DayPass
items.description: Ends the DayPass session from any menu.
items.usage_tip: Ctrl+C does the same and restores the terminal.

items.title: Help
items.description: Opens the manual of the current screen.
items.usage_tip: Enter or 0 inside a manual returns to the screen you came from; q quits DayPass.
